description: Type inference decomposed. Hindley-Milner: the foundational algorithm. Constraint generation + unification + generalisation. Extensions: type classes (Haskell), rank-N polymorphism, bidirectional type checking, subtyping, dependent types. Type variables, substitutions, principal types.

sub_mechanisms.name: type_variable
sub_mechanisms.definition: Unknown type, written α, β, etc. Introduced for unannotated expressions; gets bound during unification.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lets inference defer commitment. 'let id = λx. x' has type α → α; the specific α is determined by use. Type variables are inference's working memory.

sub_mechanisms.name: constraint_generation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Traverse AST, generate equality constraints between types. e.g., 'if e1 then e2 else e3' generates type(e1) = Bool, type(e2) = type(e3).
sub_mechanisms.why: Reduces type inference to constraint solving. Each language construct contributes specific constraints. The constraint set captures all type requirements.

sub_mechanisms.name: substitution
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mapping from type variables to types. Apply to a type by replacing variables with their mapped types.
sub_mechanisms.why: Solution to constraint set. Unification produces a substitution making all constraints satisfied. Composed substitutions accumulate as unification proceeds.

sub_mechanisms.name: occurs_check
sub_mechanisms.definition: Before binding type variable α to type T, check that α doesn't appear in T. If it does, unification fails (infinite type).
sub_mechanisms.why: Without occurs check, unification could produce α = List α — an infinite recursive type. Most languages disallow such types. Performance: O(n) check; skipping it (some implementations do) is unsound but faster.

sub_mechanisms.name: let_generalisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: After inferring let-bound expression's type, generalise free type variables to quantified ones. id : α → α becomes id : ∀α. α → α.
sub_mechanisms.why: Enables polymorphism. The generalised type can be instantiated differently at each use site. The 'let polymorphism' part of HM. Generalisation rule: only generalise variables NOT free in environment.

sub_mechanisms.name: instantiation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Replace bound type variables in ∀α. T with fresh variables. ∀α. α → α instantiates to β → β for fresh β.
sub_mechanisms.why: Each use of a polymorphic value gets its own instance. Fresh variables let different uses be independently constrained. The flip side of generalisation.

sub_mechanisms.name: principal_type
sub_mechanisms.definition: Most general type for an expression — any other valid type is an instance of it. HM finds principal types.
sub_mechanisms.why: Inference's quality measure. Principal types maximise polymorphism + composition. Damas-Milner's theorem: HM always finds principal types (when they exist).

sub_mechanisms.name: type_classes
sub_mechanisms.definition: Constrained polymorphism: types satisfying a class (e.g., Eq, Ord) can use class methods. Haskell, Rust traits, Scala implicits.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lets functions like 'sort : Ord a → [a] → [a]' work for any orderable type. Resolution: at call site, find the class instance matching the type. Coherence + global instance uniqueness required.

sub_mechanisms.name: rank_N_polymorphism
sub_mechanisms.definition: Polymorphic types nested inside other types. e.g., (∀α. α → α) → Int — function takes a polymorphic argument.
sub_mechanisms.why: Beyond HM. Useful for higher-order combinators (ST monad in Haskell). Inference becomes undecidable; requires type annotations at higher-rank positions. Haskell extensions support this.

sub_mechanisms.name: bidirectional_type_checking
sub_mechanisms.definition: Alternates between inferring (synthesis) and checking (against expected type). Useful for systems where inference is undecidable.
sub_mechanisms.why: Type annotations break the inference into local decidable problems. Used in Haskell's GHC for higher-rank types, F* / Idris / Agda for dependent types, TypeScript for contextual typing.

sub_mechanisms.name: value_restriction
sub_mechanisms.definition: OCaml/ML restriction: generalisation only on values, not arbitrary expressions. Prevents unsound polymorphism with side effects.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without it, 'let r = ref (λx. x)' would have generalised type giving unsoundness — ref's polymorphic content gets used at different types. Restriction trades expressiveness for soundness.

sub_mechanisms.name: row_polymorphism
sub_mechanisms.definition: Polymorphism over record extensions: a function works on records with at least certain fields, possibly more. OCaml objects, PureScript, GoSubtyping-style.
sub_mechanisms.why: Flexible record types without subtyping's complications. The 'extra fields' are abstracted via row variables. Used in some ML extensions; pattern Type-Level used by TypeScript's structural subtyping.

derivation_rules.name: Damas_Milner_theorem_principal_types
if: the language is HM (prenex polymorphism via let-bindings, no subtyping)
then: every well-typed expression has a principal type, found by HM inference
derivation_rules.why: Foundational soundness + completeness result. Algorithm W terminates + produces the most general type. Justifies HM as 'the right' algorithm for ML-family languages.

derivation_rules.name: occurs_check_prevents_infinite_types
then: inference may produce infinite recursive types
derivation_rules.why: Without checking that α doesn't appear in T before α := T, unification can produce α = List α. Most languages disallow these. Some Prolog implementations skip occurs check for speed and have to handle the consequences.

derivation_rules.name: let_generalisation_only_on_non_free_variables
if: a type variable α is free in the environment
then: α cannot be generalised when binding
derivation_rules.why: α being free means it has constraints from the environment. Generalising would 'forget' those constraints, producing unsound types. Standard rule preserving HM's soundness.

derivation_rules.name: rank_N_inference_undecidable
then: inference becomes undecidable; annotations are required
derivation_rules.why: HM's decidability depends on prenex polymorphism. Higher-rank polymorphism in 2nd-order lambda calculus is undecidable. Bidirectional checking with annotations restores tractability.

derivation_rules.name: type_class_resolution_via_constraint_solving
then: resolution finds an Ord instance matching α at use site
derivation_rules.why: Type classes add a constraint context to types. Resolution is constraint solving: dispatch to a specific instance dictionary. Haskell does this at compile time (no runtime overhead); Java interfaces do similar at runtime.
